subject: Veridian Labs discovery — SLOs, model requirements & topology next actions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna@veridian.ai>, Ben Wu <ben@veridian.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-08T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Veridian discovery — SLOs, model requirements & topology next actions

Hi Anna / Ben,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really valuable to see where Veridian is headed. This note captures what we heard on the call, the technical constraints you described, and proposed next steps so we all have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Tail latency spikes during business hours (p99.9) when batch jobs and interactive queries coincide — customers see timeouts on short-form generations.
- Cost sensitivity for steady-state traffic but strict p99 latency targets during peak windows.
- Mixed-model footprint: a handful of low-latency classification endpoints (short seq lengths) and a few long-form generation paths (up to ~2048 tokens) for research users.

Goals you articulated:
- p50 ~ 80–120ms for short classification calls; p99 <= 450ms for interactive UX.
- Support sustained throughput of ~450 reqs/sec for classification + burst to 2k reqs/sec for short windows.
- Ability to pin model variants (ft-13B for quality-sensitive flows; distilled 6B for fallback) and route per-route.

Technical constraints / notes from the call:
- Existing infra is multi-AZ in us-west with a small EU footprint (we'll want to propose a dual-region option for redundancy).
- KV cache hit rate is low today because many requests are short/unique — prefix caching could help for the research playground but not the classification traffic.
- Security: SOC2 evidence required; you have an in-house KMS and need audit logs for inference requests.

Initial Redwood proposal (high level):
- Dedicated pool for classification routes (optimized for latency, smaller batch sizes, pinned ft-13B quantized to int8 when validated).
- Hosted/dedicated hybrid for generation: hosted for non-sensitive research traffic; dedicated private capacity for production long-form (to bound p99).
- Enable automatic fallback to distilled 6B when latency SLOs are at risk; implement tiered routing by latency/cost policy.
- Recommend KV prefix caching for long-form flows where we see repeated prompts; otherwise rely on aggressive batching and shorter max sequence for classification routes.

Attachments: I attached the traffic sample you shared in the meeting and a first pass SLO worksheet (draft).

Next steps / asks (owners + rough due dates):
1) Veridian: confirm the traffic sample & provide a 24‑hour tail-latency log excerpt (Ben) — due 2026-09-10.
2) Redwood: produce a quick topology sketch (dual-region + dedicated pool sizing) and a cost/latency tradeoff table (Jordan + Karthik) — ETA 2026-09-11.
3) Technical deep-dive demo (live runbook + quantization experiments) — schedule the 60m deep-dive for next week; propose Wed 2026-09-15 or Thu 2026-09-16.

If that aligns, I will upload the draft SLO spreadsheet to the shared Drive and we can lock a time for the technical session.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

On Sep 8, 2026, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today — really valuable to see where Veridian is headed.

Thanks Jordan — that summary is spot on. A couple clarifications from our side that should help with sizing:
- The 450 reqs/sec baseline is an aggregate across 12 classification endpoints; each endpoint averages ~40–60 tokens per request.
- Peak windows are traffic surges triggered by partner batch jobs (~2–3x baseline lasting 10–20 minutes).
- For long-form generation, p50 is not critical but the p95/p99 must be stable for paid customers (we want <= 1.2s p99 for those flows).

Ben is attaching a 24-hour request log (anonymized) — filename is veridian-traffic-sample.csv. You should see clear bursts around 09:00–09:20 and 17:30–17:50 PST.

We agree with the hybrid approach you suggested. Regarding security: SOC2 is in progress — we can share the audit schedule and the current gap list during the next meeting.

We can do the technical deep-dive on Thu 2026-09-16 at 10am PT. That gives you a couple of days to draft the topology.

Anna Torres

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Veridian — topology & quick technical approach

Jordan / Irene — quick internal note after reading the traffic sample Anna sent. High-level technical suggestions to include in the deliverable: 

1) Model quantization and packing
- Validate int8 QAT for ft-13B; run a small A/B on a representative prompt set. If quality delta is unacceptable, fallback to 4-bit quant + per-layer fp16 for critical layers.

2) Batching policy by route
- Classification routes: target micro-batches of 4–8, max latency budget 120ms p50, p99 <= 450ms. Use preemption rules to drain long-form generation requests.
- Long-form routes: larger batch windows (50–150ms) but capped max sequence length to reduce token compute cost.

3) Topology sketch (proposed)
- Dedicated us-west pool (4–8x A100-equivalent nodes) sized for baseline classification throughput with autoscale headroom for 2–3x bursts.
- Warm standby in eu-west (2–3 nodes) for failover + regulatory use-cases.
- Hybrid: use hosted Redwood for non-sensitive research tenants to avoid overprovisioning dedicated capacity.

4) Caching & KV usage
- Introduce short-lived prefix cache for long-form research playground; not recommended for classification due to low locality.

5) SLA mechanics
- Propose route-level SLOs with fallback routing and an automated alerting hook for p99 breaches. Also include a cost cap that triggers degraded-quality fallbacks (distilled model) during sustained breaches.

I'll draft the quick sizing calc and expected cost delta for int8 vs fp16 and have that ready for Jordan's deliverable on 2026-09-11.

-karthik
